name: Dakar
subtitle: Dakar, capital of Senegal: its numbers, a short history and places to see beyond the World Heritage list.

keyPoints.text: About 1,278,471 people live in the département of Dakar (the core city, without its suburbs) (counted 2023).

parts.text: Before the French arrived, the Cape Verde peninsula, where Dakar stands, had been occupied by the Lebu people since the end of the 14th century.
In 1857 a French ship's captain, Protêt, took possession of Dakar and on 25 May declared the place a French possession.
Colonists began moving from over-populated Gorée to the fishing village of Dakar, which had a natural deep port.
In 1902 the capital of French West Africa moved from Saint-Louis to Dakar.
Dakar's population rose from 3,000 in 1869 to 18,000 in 1904 and 214,000 in 1945.
The Dakar region lies at the extreme west of the Cap-Vert peninsula, on the Atlantic coast, and covers about 550 km2.
Since June 1958 the Dakar region has been the seat of government and the capital of the country.
The Pointe des Almadies, at the north-west of the Cap-Vert peninsula, is the westernmost point of the African continent.
The Port of Dakar handled 29.66 million tonnes of traffic in 2025, up from 24.58 million tonnes the year before.
In the Dakar region 68.7% of residents aged 3 and over often use Wolof.
The Dakar Biennale of contemporary African art was set up in 1989; its 1992 edition was the first devoted to the visual arts.
The Dakar Biennale's 1996 edition began a series reserved exclusively for the visual arts of Africa and its diaspora.

blocks.prompt: About how many people do you think live in the département of Dakar (the core city, without its suburbs)?

parts.text: 1,278,471 in 2023, according to the figures compiled from the national statistics office. Which area is counted matters: Département de Dakar (the core city: its 79 km2 area, without Pikine, Guédiawaye, Keur Massar or Rufisque); the wider Dakar region counted 4,004,426 inhabitants.

items.text: The Lebu people occupied the Cape Verde peninsula, where Dakar now stands.
Captain Protêt took possession of Dakar for France and declared it a French possession on 25 May.
The railway between Dakar and Saint-Louis was built, which secured the success of the town.
The capital of French West Africa moved from Saint-Louis to Dakar.
Dakar's first master plan was drawn up, creating the modern city with the Allées du Centenaire.
The first World Festival of Black Arts took place in Dakar, where Senghor launched the idea of a museum of Black civilisations.
The Island of Gorée, off Dakar, was inscribed on UNESCO's World Heritage List.
The Dakar Biennale held its first edition devoted to the visual arts.
The African Renaissance Monument was unveiled on 3 April, the day before Senegal's 50th independence anniversary.
The Museum of Black Civilisations was inaugurated by President Macky Sall, seven years after works began under Abdoulaye Wade.
Excavators began to demolish the Sandaga market building so that the authorities could rebuild and modernise it.
The fifth national census counted 4,004,426 inhabitants in the Dakar region.

blocks.q: Myth or fact: Gorée is often presented as the centre of the transatlantic slave trade.
blocks.explain: UNESCO's own Courier notes that the central role of the island in the history of the transatlantic slave trade is now debated, even though its House of Slaves became the emblem of that history.
